findings.title: Density-signal sketch passes capped `filtered_counts`, contradicting the pre-cap requirement
findings.description: The design states three times that the dispatch signal must be pre-cap: line 27 ("the density signal for dispatch reads the CSR's raw `counts` output — not anything capped"), line 116 ("recorded from the CSR `filtered_counts` (post-`exclude_self`, pre-cap)"), and line 409. But both implementation sketches — the Tick Integration step 8 (lines 158–159) and the Data Flow (line 251) — call `spatial.record_density(filtered_counts)` at the *end* of the tick. In the current pipeline (`src/migratory/engine/tick.py:66-75`), `apply_neighbor_cap` **rebinds** `filtered_flat, filtered_counts` whenever any profile sets `max_neighbors`, so at end-of-tick that name holds capped counts. The design's flagship verification scenario (walkthrough step 5: `test.yaml`, `max_neighbors=1`) is exactly cap-active — the signal would collapse to ≈1.0, the dispatcher would lock onto grid after tick 1, and the stated behavior ("brute_selected dominates" in steady state) would never occur. An implementer following the sketch implements the wrong signal. Fix: capture the post-`exclude_self` counts *before* the cap step (or pass the raw `counts`), and name the variable so it cannot be confused with the rebound name.

findings.title: Bit-exact parity criterion contradicts set-level parity and is unachievable as written
findings.description: The design correctly asserts order-insensitive parity at unit level — line 431 ("order within a row may differ for grid, so compare as sets") and line 329 ("same CSR neighbor sets") — but step 5 of the Development Approach demands an integration test that "confirms **bit-exact position equality** against brute-force-only over N ticks" while "exercis[ing] both backends in one run." Verified in source: `BruteForceQuery.query_radius_batch` emits each row in ascending agent-index order (`np.nonzero` column order), while `HashGridQuery.query_radius_batch` emits rows in 3×3 cell-gather order. Downstream, `np.add.reduceat` sums in edge order (`src/migratory/engine/flocking.py` `_csr_reduceat`), so different row orders give different floating-point rounding; `apply_neighbor_cap`'s `np.argpartition` selection is also input-order dependent at distance ties (its own docstring admits ties are "not stable"). Positions therefore diverge bitwise from a brute-force-only baseline shortly after the first grid tick — the test as specified cannot pass (or would only pass vacuously with no switch). The same contradiction invalidates walkthrough step 1's claim that "any divergence indicates a dispatcher correctness bug" for multi-tick tests that trigger a switch. Related gap: the slice never restates what the architecture's *tick determinism* goal means under dispatch, and walkthrough step 2 defers to "documented determinism caveats in the hash grid" that exist nowhere (slice 105, `hash_grid.py`, and the perf journal document no such caveats). The design must either specify a canonical per-row ordering in the dispatcher (noting its cost) or relax parity to tolerance/statistical equivalence and state the determinism contract explicitly (identical output across repeated runs given identical dispatch decisions; not bit-identical across backends).

findings.title: `record_density` failure modes unenumerated — division by zero on empty evaluation
findings.description: The tick→dispatcher density feedback is the only new message type this slice introduces, but its degenerate inputs are not enumerated. The specified computation `float(counts.sum()) / len(counts)` divides by zero when the tick runs with an empty active subset — a legal input under the architecture's subset-evaluable tick contract (the tick function early-returns only when `n == 0`, not when `eval_indices` is empty; `exclude_self` then returns empty arrays). The result is either a `ZeroDivisionError` or a NaN that silently poisons the threshold comparison and backend selection — the latter violates the project rule "never use silent fallback values; fail explicitly." The first-tick case is handled; the empty-evaluation case is not. Specify explicit handling (e.g., skip recording and retain the previous signal, or raise) and add it to the edge-case list alongside "first tick" and "hysteresis at exactly t ± h."

findings.title: Concrete backend types in `AdaptiveSpatial.__init__` weaken the stated extensibility claim
findings.description: The constructor is typed `grid: HashGridQuery, brute: BruteForceQuery`, while the doc sells the pattern as "future spatial backends (KD-tree, GPU-accelerated) slot into `AdaptiveSpatial` ... with no protocol change" and the architecture principle (and CLAUDE.md) is to program to interfaces. Typing the slots as `SpatialQuery` with role-neutral names costs nothing and makes the extensibility claim honest; today a third backend requires editing `adaptive.py`'s signature as well as its wiring.

findings.title: "Moves from `server.py`" misstates the current state of the cell-size derivation
findings.description: Slice 105's outcome note records "Server wiring reverted to `BruteForceQuery()`", and the construction site is still `server.py:127` (`spatial=BruteForceQuery()`) with no `cell_size` derivation anywhere in `src/migratory_server/` (verified by grep). The derivation logic will be *added* to `server.py`, not moved out of it; an implementer looking for existing logic to extract will find none. The described behavior itself (fallback to `max(world.width, world.height)` for the empty-profile edge case) accurately carries over slice 105's proven caveat, so this is a wording correction only.
